Scope the release dry run's ref check to refs it can move (#290)

Step 6 of tools/release-dry-run.sh no longer compares a hash of the
whole git for-each-ref listing. It compares 2 snapshots of these refs,
taken before the run and in step 6 from the worktree that holds the
script: the branch that HEAD names, or the word detached; the commit
that HEAD resolves to; and every tag and note with its object name. On
a mismatch it prints both snapshots, so the failure names the ref that
differs. A leak check then fails the run when a ref that git
for-each-ref lists from that worktree contains the dry-run commit. The
script's header states what step 6 proves, how the script makes and
reads the dry-run commit, and which programs, attribute files and
filter drivers its git calls keep out of reach. The run fails whenever
one of the script's own checks fails, or a tool that the script calls
refuses or fails, unless the script handles that outcome itself. So a
check or a tool call that this change adds can fail a run that passed
before. Examples of such checks, not a full list, are the leak check,
the check that git refuses a GIT_ATTR_SOURCE that names no tree with
exit 128 and its own message, and the check that the next sentence
states. The run fails when a name holds an equals sign among the filter
driver names that it turns off: the name inside each filter setting
that git config lists from the script's worktree, the rest of each word
of the info/attributes file that starts with filter=, and each value
that git check-attr prints for the filter attribute of a path of the
dry-run commit; so a word of the info/attributes file that starts with
filter= and holds another equals sign fails the run, even in a comment.

The new suite tools/test-release-dry-run-refs.py runs the whole
script, with stand-ins for its tools, in throwaway folders; its
docstring states how each of its 74 cases is built and what it
requires. .github/workflows/release-dry-run.yml and
tools/run_all_checks.sh run it before the dry run, and SCRIPT_SHA256
in tools/test-run-all-checks.py records the sha256 of the changed
tools/run_all_checks.sh. tools/test-version-selectors.sh now runs the
dry run's version selector in its new form, after the script's own git
settings, and requires each of its 4 structural checks to run once for
each of its 3 sites. The change also adds .github/squash/290.txt, its
squash message.

A ref that git for-each-ref lists, moved by another worktree of the
same repository during the run, changed the old hash and failed the
dry run, although the dry run had moved nothing. TODO 279 asks for a
comparison of only the refs that the dry run could itself move, after
such a failure on the PR 284 gate; it does not record which ref moved
there, so whether this change would have avoided that failure is
unknown.

This narrows a release-integrity check on purpose and needs the
maintainer's acceptance. The script still publishes nothing: it holds
no gh call and no git push. release-dry-run.yml keeps its permissions
and its other steps. What step 6 no longer catches, and what it does
not see, is the header's residual, the first of the copies below.

The suite's text case requires the paragraphs and sentences below,
copied from the script's comments and the suite's docstring, to appear
here word for word:

Residual: the proof does not catch the deletion of any ref outside
tags and notes other than the branch the script's worktree has checked
out, such as another branch, a remote-tracking ref, refs/stash or a
refs/replace/ ref; or a move or creation of such a ref at a commit
that does not contain the dry-run commit, at an annotated tag that
peels to such a commit, or at an object that peels to no commit, such
as a tree or a blob. It does not see the HEAD or the per-worktree refs
of any worktree other than the script's worktree, the throwaway
worktree included, or a ref outside refs/ other than HEAD, such as
ORIG_HEAD, of any worktree, the script's worktree included, so such a
ref put on the dry-run commit does not fail it. It does not see a
write to a ref made after the after snapshot, such as a tag that
another worktree makes then, other than a ref that the leak check,
which follows that snapshot, finds to contain the dry-run commit. It
does not see anything the exit cleanup does, or a ref moved and then
restored between the 2 snapshots. None of these limits holds for a ref
whose name git rejects, that git for-each-ref would list from the
script's worktree and that is there when a listing of the run meets
it, as the tag and note listing of each snapshot meets a tag or a note
and the listing of the leak check meets any such ref: such a ref fails
the run, whoever writes it and whenever, at the first listing that
meets it, where the run ends, since git writes a warning to standard
error while that listing runs.

So no filter runs during a git call of the dry run, whatever the
configuration that git reads in any worktree defines, other than a
driver that the info/attributes file, or the tree that git archive
archives, comes to name during the run.

The git calls of the tools that the script runs are covered only by
the lazy-fetch, attribute and filter settings.

Residual of the test: stand-ins replace the packaging, the gates and
the site rewrite, which the next step of release-dry-run.yml runs with
the real tools, and the script runs with an environment that the test
fixes, with a git stand-in first on PATH in the ref cases and a git
wrapper there in some other cases, not with those of that workflow. A
change to the script is caught only when it changes what a case
observes, so a change that acts only outside the cases, such as one
that tests for the stand-ins or for the workflow's environment, or that
moves a ref no case writes or stops step 6 reading one, is not caught.
The text case does not catch a paragraph added next to a block, words
added next to a repeated sentence, a copy changed so far that its words
are less than 85 percent alike to those of the sentence it copies, a
fact restated in other words, a change in a text that it does not
read, or a change to a text that the checkout lacks, as CI lacks
PR-BODY.md and SQUASH-MSG. The cases run on 1 git version with its
default ref backend.

The tag and note listing of each snapshot and the listing of the leak
check fail the run when git writes anything to standard error while it
lists, as when git for-each-ref skips a ref whose name it rejects, with
a warning, and still exits 0. A ref that another worktree writes during
the run fails the proof only when it is a tag or a note, when it is the
HEAD of the script's worktree or the branch that worktree has checked
out, when it is a ref that git for-each-ref lists from the script's
worktree, created or moved onto the dry-run commit or a descendant of
it, or when git fails or writes to standard error while it lists the
refs of a snapshot or of the leak check, as it does for a ref whose
name it rejects; any other such write is outside the proof. In a
shallow clone, the leak check, which reads with the shallow file turned
off, finds the parents of a commit at the shallow boundary missing, so
there it can fail the run on git's message about them or naming a ref
that does not contain the dry-run commit; release-dry-run.yml checks
out the whole history, so its run is not shallow. Before it goes on or
fails, the run clears the name of the temporary file of the check of
GIT_ATTR_SOURCE, so that the exit cleanup cannot remove a file that
another process makes later under that name, and then tries to remove
the file itself, and fails if that removal fails; a signal that ends
the run between that clearing and that removal, or a failure of that
removal, leaves the file behind, since the exit cleanup then has no
name to remove.

The suite's trace2 case reads git's trace2 log of a run. It requires
every run of git that the script starts after the before snapshot,
other than a run in the form of the reads of the 2 snapshots or of the
leak check, to run with the attribute and filter settings, except 4,
each in the argument form that the script gives it: the first 3, which
run before those settings exist, and the check of GIT_ATTR_SOURCE,
which sets its own. Each of those 4 is exempt from these settings only
in the argument form and with the GIT_ATTR_SOURCE that the script gives
it, and only once, so a later run in that form must run with them. A
run in the form of those reads is a git symbolic-ref, rev-parse or
for-each-ref given -C and the path of the main worktree first, or a git
call given --contains; the case reads every such run as one of those
reads, wherever the script makes it, so it does not show that the
script makes such a call only in the 2 snapshots and the leak check.

The checks that ran, and the line that each ended with, are in the
description of pull request 290.
